analytics.ai_overview:
🔊
High-level summary: For Arijit Singh, vocals dominate the audio-stem similarity signal at 93.79% of total feature importance. Instrumental stems together contribute the remaining ~6.21%.
🎤
Vocals (93.79%) — primary driver: Similarity is largely determined by vocal characteristics (timbre, pitch contour, phrasing, vibrato, articulation). Prioritize vocal features such as MFCCs, pitch/f0 tracks, spectral envelope, formants and temporal dynamics for nearest-neighbor or embedding models.
🎸
Guitar (2.55%) and Drums (2.24%) — secondary context: These stems supply harmonic and rhythmic context that refines matches (arrangement, groove, acoustic vs. produced). Include them to disambiguate tracks with similar vocals but different accompaniments.
🎹
Piano (0.07%) — negligible on average: Piano contributes almost no weight to the global similarity signal for this artist. It may still matter for specific piano-driven tracks, so consider conditional handling rather than global emphasis.
🎚️
Bass (0.38%) and Other (0.97%) — low but useful: These stems are minor on average but can be important for distinguishing production styles or subgenres (e.g., strong bass in electronic/pop arrangements).
⚖️
Model-weighting recommendation: Use a default weighting that heavily favors vocals (~0.94) but expose per-query controls or modes (e.g., "vocal-first", "arrangement-aware") so users can increase instrumental influence when needed.
🔍
Feature extraction suggestions: For vocals focus on f0/pitch contours, timbral embeddings, MFCC deltas, and prosodic features. For instruments include chroma/harmonic features, onset/rhythm features, and per-stem energy envelopes to capture arrangement differences.
⚠️
Caveats & evaluation: Heavy vocal weighting risks matching by singer identity rather than song similarity (e.g., same singer across different songs). Mitigate with test sets that include covers, multiple singers, and instrumentation variants; consider ensemble models or normalization strategies to reduce bias.
